newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees record holiday sales.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees record holiday sales.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. expects record holiday sales this year, keyed by a broad range of merchandise, particularly clothes and tools, a company official said Wednesday.
The official, John Costello, senior executive vice president of marketing, said sales gains have been broadly based throughout the store and across the country.
Costello said in a telephone interview that sales through the week ended Dec. 8 met internal plans of Sears, which is based in the Chicago suburb of Hoffman Estates, Ill.
Apparel was performing well across a wide range of categories, and the company's hard goods such as Craftsman tools, computers, and seasonal items were also selling well, Costello said.
Despite a lagging consumer electronics retailing sector, Costello said Sears has posted increases in electronics sales versus a year ago, with computers leading the way.
In 1995, Sears fourth-quarter sales accounted for $10.9 billion of its annual $34.9 billion sales, and $455 million of its $1.8 billion in net income.
Arthur Martinez, Sears chairman had said in an interview in late November, that he expected same-store retail sales to be up about six percent from a year ago.
